rows.note: This is the all-purpose casual choice for someone being held in a police or prison context, though it can also mean a criminal or suspect.

example.english: They are still a prisoner and cannot be released on bail yet.
example.traditional: 佢而家仲係犯人，未可以保釋。
example.jyutping: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 zung6 hai6 faan6 jan4 mei6 ho2 ji5 bou2 sik1

rows.note: Use this for a captured person, especially an enemy or prisoner of war, rather than an ordinary jail inmate.

example.traditional: 呢名俘虜將會被送返原居地。
example.jyutping: nei1 ming4 fu1 lou5 zoeng1 wui5 bei6 sung3 faan1 jyun4 geoi1 dei6

rows.note: Use this when the prisoner is a hostage: someone held to force another person or side to comply.

example.english: The kidnappers are holding a prisoner hostage and demanding money from the bank.
example.traditional: 綁匪挾持咗一名人質，要求銀行交錢。
example.jyutping: bong2 fei2 hip3 ci4 zo2 jat1 ming4 jan4 zi3 jiu1 kau4 ngan4 hong4 gaau1 cin2

rows.note: Use this literary metaphor for someone trapped or spiritually confined by fear or another set of circumstances.

example.english: Fear has made him a prisoner of his own life.
example.traditional: 恐懼令佢成為自己人生嘅囚徒。
example.jyutping: hung2 geoi6 ling6 keoi5 sing4 wai4 zi6 gei2 jan4 sang1 ge3 cau4 tou4
